raw.assessment: The incumbent plausibly serves stable courses well: their median handling time was seven minutes. Overall, 32/40 intended course sets and a 17-minute median miss the targets. Six affected exports coincide with reassignment, supporting investigation of current-assignment semantics, not establishing causality. The two renamed-course cases limit that explanation: apparent absence may involve name reconciliation. Execution lasts 40–75 seconds, while replacement waits are much longer; their contribution to handling minutes is unmeasured. Zero observed cross-center rows does not establish isolation for the unsampled split-course case.

openings.claim: Using current instructor assignments may select the wrong course membership for a requested week; renamed courses may instead be present under an unexpected label.
openings.delta: Distinguish actual membership errors from name-based apparent omissions before choosing an export change.
openings.prediction: Under this account, reassignment cases disagree with a stipulated weekly membership set, while rename-only cases retain membership despite changed labels.
openings.probe: Within a bounded staging session, run fabricated unchanged, reassigned, renamed and split-course fixtures with explicit expected membership. Compare internal course identity, exported rows and displayed names; include a second center and concurrent attendance entry. Preserve the documented CSV. Estimate any temporal-selection repair before committing the remaining six-day budget.
assumptions: Stable identities and sufficient assignment history may exist; this is unverified.
A repair must fit the hosting allowance and six engineer-days.

openings.claim: Would faster replacement availability reduce active handling enough, or does reconciling conflicting course lists dominate coordinator effort?
openings.delta: Measure active work separately from elapsed replacement delay.
openings.prediction: If reconciliation dominates, immediate corrected files still require substantial checking; if repeated follow-up dominates, immediate availability removes measured active work.
openings.probe: Use the six coordinators’ two short sessions for counterbalanced fabricated export tasks, with immediate versus delayed corrected-file availability. Record checking, correction, downloading, importing and follow-up minutes separately from waiting. Keep files in authorized workspaces and ordinary attendance entry available.
assumptions: Fabricated tasks approximate real handling sufficiently to guide, not establish, the next-40-export success claim.

raw.assessment: Assignment changes and renames correlate with affected exports, but neither query failure nor spreadsheet interpretation is established. The observed 80% course-set accuracy and 17-minute median miss the targets. The sampled absence of cross-center rows does not cover course splits.

openings.claim: A course could disappear because export eligibility follows its current instructor rather than its identity during the requested week. Selecting center-owned course-week membership independently of instructor assignment could preserve historical attendance.
openings.delta: Make instructor reassignment irrelevant to historical course inclusion; explicitly retain intended courses with zero attendance rather than deriving the roster solely from attendance rows.
openings.prediction: With week, course membership and attendance held constant, changing only the current instructor changes the incumbent export's course set; an identity-based selector remains invariant.
openings.probe: Use fabricated staging participants to replay reassignment, rename and split cases, including concurrent attendance entry and neighboring-center records. Compare internal course identities and documented-schema CSVs. Restrict any subsequent patch to existing resources and six engineer-days; verify zero-attendance inclusion and center isolation before release.
assumptions: Recoverable course-week membership exists independently of current instructor assignments.
A bounded selector change can satisfy the engineering, hosting and concurrent-entry limits.

openings.claim: Are some reported missing courses already present in the CSV but become unrecognizable or merged during spreadsheet import after renaming or splitting?
openings.delta: Locate the first point where an intended course disappears: service selection, CSV representation, spreadsheet import or coordinator recognition.
openings.prediction: An interpretation/import failure leaves the intended course's fabricated attendance in the raw CSV while its recognizable representation disappears downstream; a selector failure omits those records before download.
openings.probe: In the six coordinators' short sessions, trace distinct fabricated attendance markers through raw files and their usual imports for unchanged, renamed and split courses. Record checking, importing and correction times separately, entirely within authorized workspaces. Preserve the CSV schema and ordinary attendance access.
assumptions: Fabricated examples can reproduce coordinators' usual import behavior.
Distinct record markers fit the documented schema without modification.

openings.claim: Current-instructor eligibility may omit historical courses; center-owned course-week selection should retain intended zero-attendance courses.
openings.discriminator: Hold week, membership and attendance constant; change only current instructor.
openings.probe: Compare identities and CSV rows for fabricated unchanged, reassigned, renamed and split courses; test zero attendance, neighboring-center isolation and concurrent entry.
openings.uncertainty: Recoverable history, stable identities and bounded repair cost unverified; correlation is not causation.

openings.claim: Renamed or split courses may disappear during representation, import or recognition despite existing CSV records.
openings.discriminator: Locate first loss across selection, CSV, spreadsheet and recognition.
openings.fit: Preserves constraints using authorized fabricated tasks.
openings.probe: Trace distinct schema-compatible attendance markers through usual imports; measure checking, importing and correction.
openings.uncertainty: Marker compatibility and realistic reproduction unverified; split-center isolation unsampled.

openings.uncertainty: Timetable completeness/update timing and real-world task representativeness remain unknown.

post_distill.decision: Run bounded probes before selecting a repair. Keep participant names private/in authorized workspaces, documented CSV supported, attendance entry available, and changes within six engineer-days/current hosting. Coordinate sessions within available resources. Staging cannot establish success: next 40 exports must achieve median handling ≤12 minutes, ≥95% intended course sets and zero foreign-center records.
